      (q.1 : ℂ) A D w) z - branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch *
      (C*cuspPowerResponse (branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch) (q.1 : ℂ) A D z) =
    C*(A*(z 1 : ℂ)^(q.1 : ℂ)+D*(z 1 : ℂ)^(1-(q.1 : ℂ)))^2

    hyperbolicLaplacian (fun w => C*cuspPowerResponse (branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch)
      (q.1 : ℂ) A D w) z - branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch *
      (C*cuspPowerResponse (branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch) (q.1 : ℂ) A D z) =
    C*(A*(z 1 : ℂ)^(q.1 : ℂ)+D*(z 1 : ℂ)^(1-(q.1 : ℂ)))^2

by
  have hp := ((powerResponse_smooth (branchParameter (q.1 : ℂ) minusBranch)
    (2*(q.1 : ℂ)) (A^2) z hz).add

  rw [hyperbolicLaplacian_const_mul hp C]
  have he := xi_cusp_response_equation q minusBranch A D z hz
  linear_combination C*he

theorem CuspHeightTest.zero_low (h : CuspHeightTest) {y : ℝ} (hy : y ≤ 2) : h.field y = 0 :=

    (h.smooth.comp Complex.imCLM.contDiff)

    tsupport h.planarField ⊆ {z : ℂ | z.re ∈ Icc (-1) 1 ∧ z.im ∈ tsupport h.field} := by

  have hr : h.field z.im ≠ 0 := by

    h.planarField_support
  support := by
    intro z hz
    have hh := h.support (h.planarField_support hz).2
    change 2 < z.im at hh
    change 0 < z.im
    linarith

def CuspLogTest.heightTest (f : CuspLogTest) : CuspHeightTest where
  field := f.heightField
  smooth := f.heightField_smooth
  compact := (f.compact.image Real.continuous_exp).of_isClosed_subset isClosed_closure
    f.heightField_support
  support := by
    intro y hy

    have hh := Real.exp_lt_exp.mpr (f.support ht)
    change 2 < Real.exp t

  funext t
  simp only [CuspHeightTest.logProfile,CuspLogTest.heightTest,CuspLogTest.heightField,
    if_pos (Real.exp_pos t),Real.log_exp,cuspLogWeight]
  rw [← mul_assoc,← Complex.ofReal_mul,← Real.exp_add]
  rw [show -t/2+t/2=0 by ring,Real.exp_zero,Complex.ofReal_one,one_mul]

    inner ℂ (f.operatorVector : Space) (g.operatorVector : Space) =

  rw [show f.operatorVector = f.heightTest.operatorVector from rfl,
    show g.operatorVector = g.heightTest.operatorVector from rfl,
    CuspHeightTest.logProfile_inner,f.logProfile_heightTest,g.logProfile_heightTest]

/-! ### Exact transfer to a quadratic-moment certificate -/

/-- A corrected quadratic Brascamp--Lieb value bound discharges the target moment inequality.
This is the algebraic consumer of the positive Popescu remainder: no uniform curvature floor is
needed once the variable-curvature value `J` and correction value `C` are retained. -/
theorem correctedQuadraticBrascampLiebCertificate
    {a₀ a₁ a₂ J C c : ℝ}
    (hvariance : a₀ * a₂ - a₁ ^ 2 ≤ 4 * a₀ * J - a₀ * C)
    (hcertificate :
      64 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * J - 16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * C ≤
        (45 - 16 * c ^ 2) * a₁ ^ 2) :
    16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * a₂ ≤ 45 * a₁ ^ 2 := by
  have hscale : 0 ≤ 16 * c ^ 2 := by positivity
  have hscaled := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hvariance hscale
  nlinarith

/-- Every uncorrected variable-curvature certificate implies the corrected certificate when the
Popescu value is nonnegative. -/
theorem correctedQuadraticCertificate_of_uncorrected
    {a₀ a₁ J C c : ℝ}
    (ha₀ : 0 ≤ a₀) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (huncorrected :
      64 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * J ≤ (45 - 16 * c ^ 2) * a₁ ^ 2) :
    64 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * J - 16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * C ≤
      (45 - 16 * c ^ 2) * a₁ ^ 2 := by
  have hcorrection : 0 ≤ 16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * C := by positivity
  linarith

/-- For positive mass and a nonzero scale, a strictly positive Popescu value gives a strict
improvement over the uncorrected left-hand side. -/
theorem correctedQuadraticCertificate_strictlyImproves
    {a₀ J C c : ℝ} (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) (hC : 0 < C) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    64 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * J - 16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * C <
      64 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * J := by
  have hcorrection : 0 < 16 * c ^ 2 * a₀ * C := by positivity
  linarith

/-! ### Orientation of the first Popescu remainder -/

/-- The two-term Popescu truncation is a lower bound whenever its resolvent remainder is
nonnegative.  This is the scalar orientation of the even truncation in Popescu's alternating
resolvent expansion. -/
theorem firstPopescuTruncation_le_variance_of_expansion
    {variance leading correction remainder : ℝ}
    (hexpansion : variance = leading - correction + remainder)
    (hremainder : 0 ≤ remainder) :
    leading - correction ≤ variance := by
  linarith

/-- Under the exact first-correction expansion, using the same two-term truncation as an upper
bound is equivalent to asserting that the resolvent remainder is nonpositive. -/
theorem variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_iff_remainder_nonpos
    {variance leading correction remainder : ℝ}
    (hexpansion : variance = leading - correction + remainder) :
    variance ≤ leading - correction ↔ remainder ≤ 0 := by
  rw [hexpansion]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- With the analytic nonnegativity of the resolvent remainder, a forward first-correction bound
can hold only in the equality case where that remainder vanishes. -/
theorem variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_iff_remainder_eq_zero
    {variance leading correction remainder : ℝ}
    (hexpansion : variance = leading - correction + remainder)
    (hremainder : 0 ≤ remainder) :
    variance ≤ leading - correction ↔ remainder = 0 := by
  rw [variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_iff_remainder_nonpos hexpansion]
  exact ⟨fun h => le_antisymm h hremainder, fun h => h.le⟩

/-- A strictly positive Popescu resolvent remainder rules out the forward inequality required to
subtract the first correction from an upper variance bound. -/
theorem not_variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_of_remainder_pos
    {variance leading correction remainder : ℝ}
    (hexpansion : variance = leading - correction + remainder)
    (hremainder : 0 < remainder) :
    ¬ variance ≤ leading - correction := by
  rw [variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_iff_remainder_nonpos hexpansion]
  exact not_le_of_gt hremainder

/-- The variance premise consumed by `correctedQuadraticBrascampLiebCertificate` is therefore
equivalent to vanishing of the first Popescu resolvent remainder, once the analytic expansion and
remainder nonnegativity are available. -/
theorem correctedQuadraticVarianceUpper_iff_popescuRemainder_eq_zero
    {a₀ a₁ a₂ J C remainder : ℝ}
    (hexpansion :
      a₀ * a₂ - a₁ ^ 2 = 4 * a₀ * J - a₀ * C + remainder)
    (hremainder : 0 ≤ remainder) :
    (a₀ * a₂ - a₁ ^ 2 ≤ 4 * a₀ * J - a₀ * C) ↔
      remainder = 0 :=
  variance_le_firstPopescuTruncation_iff_remainder_eq_zero
    hexpansion hremainder

end

/-!
# The scale calibration of a CCR family

The scale-sandwich law calibrates an abstract log-volume against a CCR family through two
hypotheses: its logarithmic scale mean is the mean energy, and its logarithmic scale variance is the
number variance.  The two are not independent.  Differentiating the first turns the second into a
statement about the family alone — the mean energy has logarithmic derivative equal to the number
variance — and that is the whole content of the calibration.

Scalar compressions with the mode-indexed unit leakage make the calibration explicit: their number
variance *equals* their mean energy, so the corpus bound `variance ≤ |I| · mean` is attained exactly
in one mode, and rescaling them by `√t` realizes the calibration pair on an actual CCR family.

* **`ccr_calibration_energy_law`** — the two calibrations are one differential law;
* **`ccrNumberVariance_scalar_eq_ccrMeanEnergy`** — equality of the two energies for scalar
  compressions;
* **`ccr_scaleSandwich_sqrtScalar`** — an unconditional instance of the scale-sandwich law.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HilbertMetric

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable section

variable {I n m : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]

/-! ## The calibration pair is one differential law -/

omit [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq n] in
/-- The mean calibration alone already differentiates: the mean energy of the family inherits the
derivative of `t · F₁ t`. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_ccrMeanEnergy_of_meanCalibration
    (A : ℝ → I → Matrix n n ℝ) {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hF₁ : ∀ t, 0 < t → HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ t) t)
    (hmean : ∀ t, 0 < t → logarithmicScaleMean F₁ t = ccrMeanEnergy (A t))
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => ccrMeanEnergy (A s)) (F₁ t + t * F₂ t) t := by
  have hprod : HasDerivAt (fun s => s * F₁ s) (1 * F₁ t + t * F₂ t) t :=
    (hasDerivAt_id t).mul (hF₁ t ht)
  have heq : (fun s => ccrMeanEnergy (A s)) =ᶠ[nhds t] fun s => s * F₁ s := by
    filter_upwards [isOpen_Ioi.mem_nhds ht] with s hs
    exact (hmean s hs).symm
  have := hprod.congr_of_eventuallyEq heq
  simpa using this

omit [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq m] in
/-- **The two scale calibrations are a single differential law of the family.**  A calibrated CCR
family has mean energy whose logarithmic derivative is the number variance; no property of the
log-volume survives beyond this. -/
theorem ccr_calibration_energy_law
    (A : ℝ → I → Matrix n n ℝ) (B : ℝ → I → Matrix n m ℝ) {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hF₁ : ∀ t, 0 < t → HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ t) t)
    (hmean : ∀ t, 0 < t → logarithmicScaleMean F₁ t = ccrMeanEnergy (A t))
    (hvariance : ∀ t, 0 < t →
      logarithmicScaleVariance F₁ F₂ t = ccrNumberVariance (A t) (B t))
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => ccrMeanEnergy (A s))
      (ccrNumberVariance (A t) (B t) / t) t := by
  have h := hasDerivAt_ccrMeanEnergy_of_meanCalibration A hF₁ hmean ht
  have hv : ccrNumberVariance (A t) (B t) / t = F₁ t + t * F₂ t := by
    rw [← hvariance t ht, logarithmicScaleVariance]
    field_simp
  rwa [hv]

/-! ## Scalar compressions -/

omit [DecidableEq I] in
/-- The Hilbert–Schmidt energy of a scalar matrix. -/
theorem matrixHilbertSchmidtEnergy_smul_one (c : ℝ) :
    matrixHilbertSchmidtEnergy (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) =
      (Fintype.card n : ℝ) * c ^ 2 := by
  have hentry : ∀ a b : n, (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) a b ^ 2 =
      if a = b then c ^ 2 else 0 := by
    intro a b
    by_cases hab : a = b <;> simp [hab]
  simp only [matrixHilbertSchmidtEnergy]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hentry a b]
  simp [Finset.sum_ite_eq, Finset.card_univ]

omit [DecidableEq I] in
/-- The mean energy of a scalar compression tuple. -/
theorem ccrMeanEnergy_scalar (c : I → ℝ) :
    ccrMeanEnergy (fun i => c i • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) =
      (Fintype.card n : ℝ) * ∑ i, (c i) ^ 2 := by
  simp only [ccrMeanEnergy]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => matrixHilbertSchmidtEnergy_smul_one (n := n) (c i),
    ← Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The leakage trace of a scalar compression against the mode-indexed unit leakage. -/
theorem ccrLeakageTrace_scalar (c : I → ℝ) (p : I × n) (a : n) :
    ccrLeakageTrace (fun i => c i • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ))
        (unitModeLeakage (I := I) (n := n)) p a =
      if p.2 = a then c p.1 else 0 := by
  obtain ⟨j, q⟩ := p
  simp only [ccrLeakageTrace, unitModeLeakage, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.mul_apply,
    Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.one_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    Prod.mk.injEq]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
